bug_description.normalized: The exact 72-byte witness is passed as the `mb_ereg()` pattern and reaches Oniguruma compilation through `php_mbregex_compile_pattern()`. While parsing the second look-behind `(?<=@!nnnnnnnnnIIIIn;{1}D?()|<x@x*xxxD|)`, `parse_bag()` allocates a `BAG_MEMORY` node for the lone capture group `()`, then registers that node as capture group 1 in `scan_env`. Parsing the third look-behind `(?<=@xxx|xxxxx\g<1>;{1}x)` creates a `NODE_CALL` for `\g<1>`, and `tune_call()` resolves that call before `tune_tree()` by copying `mem_env[1].mem_node` into `NODE_CALL_BODY`. During `tune_tree()`, the second look-behind's trailing empty alternative makes `node_char_len()` prove `ci.min == 0 && ci.min_is_sure != 0`, so `tune_look_behind()` rewrites that anchor in place with `onig_node_reset_empty(node)`. `node_reset_str()` immediately frees the old look-behind body through `node_free_body()` / `onig_node_free()`, releasing the same 72-byte `BAG_MEMORY` node that the call node still aliases. Later in the same tuning pass, `tune_anchor()` checks the third look-behind, reaches its `NODE_CALL`, and `check_node_in_look_behind()` follows the stale `NODE_CALL_BODY` pointer into `check_called_node_in_look_behind()`. That function executes `switch (NODE_TYPE(node))` on the freed `BAG_MEMORY` node, producing the saved `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 4` at `oniguruma/src/regcomp.c:3254`. The staged `patch.diff` and metadata `fixed_commit` are unrelated to this Oniguruma path, so the lifetime chain is grounded on the staged vulnerable source plus the saved allocation/free/crash stacks.

source.description: First project parser step that materializes the lone capture-group node from the witness's `()` inside the second look-behind. That node later becomes group 1, is aliased by `\g<1>`, then freed and read again.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 72-byte pattern `(?<=D|)(?<=@!nnnnnnnnnIIIIn;{1}D?()|<x@x*xxxD|)(?<=@xxx|xxxxx\g<1>;{1}x)` (SHA-256 `bc1908213bca14790b98bdcfa803525e8201569e2405601f01f556cde19d96bf`). The second look-behind contains the only capture group `()`, and the third look-behind contains `\g<1>`, so the witness itself creates both the later-freed group-1 node and the call that revisits it.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `check_called_node_in_look_behind()` receives the stale `NODE_CALL_BODY` pointer and reads the freed node header via `NODE_TYPE(node)`.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free on address ... READ of size 4` at `check_called_node_in_look_behind /src/php-src/oniguruma/src/regcomp.c:3254:11`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. When the second look-behind is proven to match the empty string, `tune_look_behind()` rewrites that anchor in place with `onig_node_reset_empty(node)`. The rewrite frees the old subtree but does not invalidate the previously resolved `NODE_CALL_BODY` alias that still points at capture group 1.
root_cause.note: The staged `patch.diff` does not touch this path; the source-grounded obligation comes from the vulnerable code and the saved free/crash stacks, which connect this rewrite to `node_reset_str()` and the later `check_called_node_in_look_behind()` read.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled capture group becomes `scan_env`'s group-1 `mem_node`, which is the exact object later copied into `NODE_CALL_BODY` for `\g<1>` and then freed.

parser_admitted.description: The exact 72-byte witness passes mbstring's encoding validation and Oniguruma parse-tree construction, so `onig_compile()` enters `tune_tree()`. Both the in-place look-behind rewrite and the later stale call-body walk happen inside this pass.
parser_admitted.condition: Stage 01 reproduced the saved ASan crash under `mb_ereg`, so the witness is accepted far enough to execute `tune_call()`, `tune_call2()`, and then `tune_tree(root, reg, 0, &scan_env)`.

coarse_trace.summary: The attacker-controlled mbstring pattern is validated for encoding and forwarded to `onig_new()` for parsing and compile-time tuning.

Parsing the second and third look-behinds materializes the lone capture-group `BAG_MEMORY` node from `()` and a separate `NODE_CALL` from `\g<1>`, then records the group node as capture group 1 in `scan_env`.
Before `tune_tree()`, subexpression-call tuning resolves the `\g<1>` call node so its `NODE_CALL_BODY` points directly to capture group 1's `BAG_MEMORY` node.

The second look-behind is proven to have a guaranteed zero-length alternative, so it is rewritten in place with `onig_node_reset_empty()`, recursively freeing its old subtree including capture group 1.

Later look-behind validation on the third anchor follows the stale `NODE_CALL_BODY` alias created for `\g<1>` back into the freed capture-group node, and `check_called_node_in_look_behind()` crashes when it reads that node's type field.

fine_trace.note: Source. Parsing the lone `()` inside the second look-behind allocates a `BAG_MEMORY` node for capture group 1. ASan's allocation stack for the later-crashed 72-byte region identifies this parser path through `node_new_memory()` and `parse_bag()`.

After the second look-behind body is parsed, this `BAG_MEMORY` node is registered as capture group 1 in `scan_env`. Later subexpression-call tuning resolves `\g<1>` by copying this exact pointer out of `mem_env[1]`.
Parsing the third look-behind's `\g<1>` materializes a separate `NODE_CALL` AST node with `gnum = 1`. This node is the later stale-use path back to capture group 1.

Before `tune_tree()`, `tune_call()` resolves the by-number subexpression call and stores capture group 1's `BAG_MEMORY` node from step 2 directly into the call node's body field. The `NODE_CALL` now aliases the same heap object that will later be freed.

When `tune_tree()` reaches the second look-behind `(?<=@!nnnnnnnnnIIIIn;{1}D?()|<x@x*xxxD|)`, the trailing empty alternative makes `node_char_len()` prove a guaranteed zero-length match. That control decision takes the in-place reset branch.

Root cause. `tune_look_behind()` rewrites the second look-behind anchor itself into an empty string node. The code does not invalidate the `NODE_CALL_BODY` alias from step 4, even though that alias still points into the old subtree.

The reset immediately frees the old look-behind body recursively. The saved free stack shows this path descending through `node_free_body()` / `onig_node_free()` to release the same 72-byte `BAG_MEMORY` allocation from step 1, but neither `mem_env[1]` nor the call node's body alias is cleared.

Later, `tune_anchor()` processes the third look-behind `(?<=@xxx|xxxxx\g<1>;{1}x)`. Its legality walk reaches the `NODE_CALL` case and passes `NODE_BODY(node)`—the stale `NODE_CALL_BODY` alias from step 4—to `check_called_node_in_look_behind()` after the free in step 7.

Sink. `check_called_node_in_look_behind()` immediately evaluates `NODE_TYPE(node)` on that freed `BAG_MEMORY` node, reading the reclaimed heap header. AddressSanitizer records this as `heap-use-after-free READ of size 4`.

allocation_context.note: The ASan allocation stack for the reclaimed 72-byte region runs `node_new -> node_new_bag -> node_new_memory -> parse_bag`, so this parser statement is the project allocation context for the later-freed node.

free_context.note: The free path originates at `node_reset_str()` and then descends through `node_free_body()` / `onig_node_free()` to release the same 72-byte `BAG_MEMORY` region.

format.name: raw mbstring regex pattern
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact 72-byte witness stored in `poc` (SHA-256 `bc1908213bca14790b98bdcfa803525e8201569e2405601f01f556cde19d96bf`). Its observed effect here is that Oniguruma parses a capture group `()` inside one look-behind as group 1, parses `\g<1>` inside a later look-behind, resolves that call to the group-1 node before `tune_tree()`, then rewrites the earlier look-behind to empty and frees the group-1 subtree before the later look-behind check follows the stale call-body pointer into `check_called_node_in_look_behind()`. This GT is grounded only for that exact witness, not a generalized class of mbstring regexes.
